title: Government reveals contractor shortlist for 24 Sussex overhaul
summary: The federal government has made a shortlist of seven contractors it is considering to renovate 24 Sussex Drive into a habitable residence once again.

image.caption: The official residence of the prime minister of Canada at 24 Sussex Drive is seen in Ottawa last summer. The residence's interior has been stripped and is in need of major renovations. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: The federal government has made a shortlist of seven contractors it is considering to renovate 24 Sussex Drive into a habitable residence once again.
Nearly $8.5M pledged so far, government set fundraising goal of $50M
Public Services and Procurement Canada revealed the shortlist in a news release on Friday. The contractors include:

items: Amico Design-Build Inc. in partnership with Hariri Pontarini Architects.
EBC Inc. in partnership with Diamond Schmitt Architects.
Ed Brunet and Associates Canada in partnership with Michael Green Architecture Inc.
Maple Reinders Constructors Ltd. in partnership with Patkau Architects Inc.
MARANT Construction Limited in partnership with Superkül/Quadrangle Architects Limited.
QMD-Graebeck in partnership with Daoust Lestage Inc.
SAJO-Lundy in partnership with ARCHITEM Inc.

blocks.text: Whichever company is successful in winning the contract will be tasked with overhauling the Gothic Revival mansion that served as the home for every prime minister from 1951 until 2015.
The winning team, according to documents obtained by CBC News, will be responsible for making the property universally accessible, handling landscaping elements and restoring heritage elements.
Prime Minister Mark Carney announced in June that the official residence will be getting a crowdfunded makeover after sitting empty for more than a decade.
The Rideau Hall Foundation, the organization in charge of fundraising, has set a goal of $50 million. As of Friday, the foundation has fundraised just under $8.5 million.
